extracted.intended_audience: librarians, graduate-school collection developers, bibliometricians and researchers using citation data
extracted.subtask_description: Create a ranked list of the 100 most-cited books for a specified time window using Science Citation Index data, with subject grouping and commentary on methodological limitations and uses for library collection development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: List is based on the Science Citation Index (SCI) citation data for a specified period (the twelve-year period 1961–1972).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly relies on SCI-recorded citations during the stated period; the counts and ranking reflect only citations recorded in that source and timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal window for counting citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations are counted only within the defined twelve-year period 1961–1972.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ranking reflects period-limited citation frequency (not lifetime citations). A book may have many more citations outside this window; users should interpret counts as period-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of included items ('books' / non-journal items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The list comprises 'non-journal' items as identified in the SCI (i.e., books/monographs/etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as a list of heavily cited non-journal works; note that items credited to editors, individual chapters, or other complex attributions may complicate inclusion/exclusion decisions (the compiler notes exclusions/attribution issues when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-grouping to avoid cross-field unfairness
rubrics_metrics.description: To obviate cross-field comparison unfairness, the 100 books are divided into three subject groups: Physics & Chemistry (42 items), Biochemistry & Bio-Medicine (29 items), and Mathematics & Statistics (29 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group-division is used to make comparisons fairer across disciplines; users should compare within subject groups rather than across them for meaningful interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking is approximate; group membership more important than exact rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Books are 'ranked' by citation frequency but the compiler warns against giving too much weight to an individual book's precise rank — the listing is primarily a group listing rather than an exact ordinal evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the list as indicating a 'core' group of important works rather than as a definitive absolute ordering; small differences in counts should not be over-interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biases and limitations due to source coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The list 'carries whatever bias' is inherent in its source (the SCI); coverage limitations and biases of the citation index affect which works appear and their counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must be cognizant that SCI coverage (e.g., journal selection, language coverage, regional/copyright differences) shapes results; the compiler explicitly cautions about coverage-induced bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of editions, retitling, translations and separate-language citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised editions, retitling, translations (e.g., Russian editions) and separate-language citations can fragment citation counts and affect a work's apparent ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting counts or compiling similar lists, reconcile citations across editions/titles/translations where feasible; the compiler gives examples (e.g., Smith’s Kidney/Principles of Renal Physiology, Bellamy’s infrared spectra being cited more in Russian).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling near-boundary and duplicate items; possibility of future updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial list is subject to later identification of duplicates or near-boundary items and may be supplemented or updated when such cases are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the published list as preliminary; maintain procedures for reviewing borderline cases and for adding corrections or supplements in later updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical use for libraries and collection development
rubrics_metrics.description: The list is presented as a convenience core collection for developing graduate-school libraries and as a useful starting point for growing or smaller libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Librarians may use the list to guide acquisition (especially in developing-country or small college contexts) or solicitation of donations, but should adapt purchases to local specialties and needs and prune collections accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of updating and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The compiler indicates that lists update frequently and that periodic re-compilation is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a schedule or method for periodic re-evaluation of citation-based core lists to reflect changing citation patterns and newly identified attribution issues.
